❯ Read CLAUDE.md, /docs/changelog.md, and /docs/requirements.md before          
  starting. This is a major architectural pivot — read carefully.               
                                                                                
  ## Direction change                                                           
                                                                                
  We're abandoning the custom-coded questionnaire. The survey now lives in      
  Tally at https://tally.so/r/RGZO7p, embedded as an iframe at /questionnaire.  
  On submit, Tally will redirect to /result with URL parameters carrying        
  answers (the redirect mapping is configured in Tally separately, not in this  
  codebase). /result reads those params, generates the strip, calls /api/grace, 
   displays.                                                                    
                                                                                
  This session is the architectural cleanup. Do NOT touch the strip             
  visualization or Grace prompt — visual system is being updated separately,    
  and we don't yet know the exact Tally param names.                            
                                                                                
  ## Embed code                                                                 
                                                                                
  The Tally embed:                                                              
  <iframe data-tally-src="https://tally.so/r/RGZO7p?transparentBackground=1"    
  width="100%" height="100%" frameborder="0" marginheight="0" marginwidth="0"   
  title="Creative Provenance"></iframe>                                         
                                                                                
  Plus the loader script: <script async                                         
  src="https://tally.so/widgets/embed.js"></script>                             
                                                                                
  Implement using next/script with strategy="afterInteractive" in a client      
  component. Page should be full-viewport, no header, no chrome.                
                                                                                
  ## Tasks                                                                      
                                                                                
  1. Replace /app/questionnaire/* with a single /app/questionnaire/page.tsx     
  that renders the Tally embed full-screen.                                     
                                                                                
  2. Delete (no longer needed):                                                 
     - /app/questionnaire/[step]/ (entire directory)                            
     - /app/questionnaire/layout.tsx                                            
     - /components/questions/ (entire directory)                                
     - /components/shared/StepNav.tsx                                           
     - /components/shared/MultiSelectCard.tsx                                   
     - /lib/context.tsx                                                         
     - /lib/steps.ts                                                            
     - /lib/hooks/useRovingTabIndex.ts                                          
                                                                                
  3. Update /app/page.tsx — keep CTA pointing at /questionnaire, light copy     
  adjustments OK, don't redesign.                                               
                                                                                
  4. Scaffold /app/result/page.tsx as a client component:                       
     - Use useSearchParams() to read URL params                                 
     - Define `parseTallyParams(params: URLSearchParams):                       
  Partial<ProvenanceResponse>` as a stub that returns {} for now — we'll fill   
  in the mapping once Tally redirect is configured                              
     - Render a placeholder: "Result page — awaiting param wiring and visual    
  system update"                                                                
     - Show the raw params in a debug block at the bottom (visible in dev only) 
   so I can verify the redirect works once configured                           
     - Do NOT call /api/grace yet                                               
                                                                                
  5. Update /lib/schema.ts to match the new Tally-driven shapes:                
     - Q3 references: flat array of {id: ReferenceTileId, weight: number} where 
   weight is 0.2 | 0.5 | 0.85. Drop the `position` field entirely.              
     - Q6 aiHelpers: remove 'none' from the AIHelperType union. Empty array     
  signals "no helpers used."                                                    
     - Q8 directionExecution: change from {x, y} normalized 0-1 to a single     
  integer 1-10. Just `directionExecution: number`.                              
     - Q9 collaborators: remove 'just-me' from the CollaboratorType union.      
  Empty array signals "just me."                                                
     - Q10 ownership: feltOwnership is now integer 1-10 instead of 0-1.         
     - Update Zod schemas to match.                                             
     - Add a header comment noting these shapes are the target — Tally params   
  will be mapped into them by parseTallyParams.                                 
                                                                                
  6. Update /api/grace/route.ts: leave the stub but ensure it still typechecks  
  against the new schema. Don't implement generation yet.                       
                                                                                
  7. Documentation:                                                             
     - /docs/changelog.md: new session entry describing the pivot, what was     
  deleted, what's stubbed                                                       
     - /docs/requirements.md: update Q3, Q6, Q8, Q9, Q10 schema sections;       
  rewrite the "Core User Flow" section to describe Tally embed → redirect with  
  params → /result; mark the spatial canvas + custom drag UI as deprecated/V2   
     - /docs/bugs.md: add a "Resolved by removal" section listing the           
  custom-questionnaire bugs that no longer apply                                
     - /docs/backlog.md: add "Re-implement reflective custom UI in Next.js      
  (V2)" so the original ambition isn't lost                                     
     - CLAUDE.md: remove deleted dirs from the file structure diagram; update   
  "What to Prioritize" to the new shorter scope; add a "Tally integration"      
  section explaining embed + redirect flow + planned webhook (V2)               
                                                                                
  8. Run `npm run build` and fix all type errors caused by the schema changes.  
  Build must pass cleanly.                                                      
                                                                                
  ## Constraints                                                                
                                                                                
  - No new strip rendering code. Visual system is changing.                     
  - No new Grace prompt or generation logic. Wait for the real schema flow.     
  - No webhook handler — that's a separate task after Tally redirect is         
  configured.                                                                   
  - Don't guess Tally param names; parseTallyParams is a stub.                  
  - Don't add new dependencies.

      11 -1. **Landing page** — sets context, names the project, has one 
         -CTA: "Begin"                                                   
      12 -2. **Questionnaire** — 10 questions, ~5–7 minutes, mobile-respo
         -nsive                                                          
      13 -3. **Loading state** — fingerprint composition + Grace generati
         -on (~3–8 seconds)                                              
      14 -4. **Result page** — fingerprint, Grace, download/share, "begin
         - again" option                                                 
      11 +1. **Landing page** — sets context, names the project, has one 
         +CTA: "Begin" → /questionnaire                                  
      12 +2. **Questionnaire** — Tally form (https://tally.so/r/RGZO7p) e
         +mbedded full-viewport at /questionnaire as an iframe via Tally'
         +s official embed script. ~5–7 minutes, mobile-responsive (Tally
         + handles all the question UI, validation, and accessibility).  
      13 +3. **Submit redirect** — Tally is configured (in its dashboard,
         + not in this codebase) to redirect to /result with the user's a
         +nswers as URL parameters on submit.                            
      14 +4. **Result page** — /result reads URL params, calls `parseTall
         +yParams()` to coerce them into a `ProvenanceResponse`, generate
         +s the fingerprint, calls /api/grace for the Grace text, and off
         +ers download/share.

         + Session 12 to ship faster for the symposium. Re-implementing i

  Decisions you should review

  - lib/storage.ts is now orphaned. Nothing imports it after the pivot. I kept
  it (it wasn't in your delete list and may be useful for caching the parsed
  response or Grace), but you can delete it cleanly if you don't expect to need
  it. Same goes for the now-empty components/shared/ and lib/hooks/ directories.
  - /api/grace/route.ts accepts a Partial<ProvenanceResponse> body but does
  nothing with it (consumed via void _body). This is purely to keep the route's
  typing tied to the schema so future-me can't drift.
  - /questionnaire iframe sets both data-tally-src and src — src makes the form
  visible immediately on first paint, and the embed script still picks up
  data-tally-src for resize/messaging. Slight redundancy; you can drop src if
  you'd rather defer rendering until the script runs.
  - Q3 weight as literal union (0.2 | 0.5 | 0.85) — strict, but parseTallyParams
   will need to coerce Tally's string values into one of those three literals or
   the Zod schema will reject. Loosening to z.number() is the easy fallback if
  Tally produces unexpected values.
  - Q6 + Q9 "no helpers" / "just me" encoded as empty arrays — semantically
  different from "user didn't see the question," and an empty array typechecks
  the same as a missing required answer. If you want Tally to enforce a "did the
   user see this" gate, consider a separate boolean (e.g. aiHelpers: { saw: 
  boolean; selected: AIHelperType[] }) — happy to do that pass if you want.
  - docs/backlog.md "Custom domain" entry — I struck it through with ~~, which
  renders as crossed-out in GitHub. If you'd rather just delete the line, easy
  follow-up.
  - docs/opening-prompt.md still says "Creative Provenance" in 2 places. Treated
   as historical (matching the changelog rule). Tell me if you'd rather rename
  it or move it under a /docs/historical/ subfolder.

       7 +  - `fetchSubmission(submissionId)` — GETs `https://api.tally.s
         +o/forms/RGZO7p/submissions/{submissionId}` with `Authorization:
         + Bearer ${TALLY_API_KEY}`. Throws a 404 error (with `.status` f
         +lag) if the submission isn't found, otherwise propagates a gene
         +ric error.                                                     
       8 +  - On the first successful call per process, logs the raw resp
         +onse shape to the server console so we can inspect it and refin
         +e the mapping.                                                 
       9 +  - `mapTallyToProvenance(submission)` — best-effort map from T
         +ally's `fields`/`responses` array to `Partial<ProvenanceRespons
         +e>`. Uses label/key substring heuristics to find each question,
         + resolves option IDs to text via the field's `options` table, a
         +nd matches against the schema's literal unions. TODO comments m
         +ark fields whose exact Tally shape can't be confirmed without a
         + real submission (notably Q3's per-tile bucket fields and Q7's 
         +branch presence).                                              
      10 +- Created `app/api/tally-submission/route.ts` — GET handler. Re
         +ads `sid` from the query string, calls `fetchSubmission` + `map
         +TallyToProvenance`, returns the mapped response as JSON. 400 if
         + `sid` is missing, 404 if the submission isn't found, 500 for o
         +ther errors.                                                   
      11 +- Updated `app/result/page.tsx`:                               
      12 +  - Removed `parseTallyParams`. The result page no longer reads
         + form answers from URL params — only `sid`.

⏺ Summary of all changes

  Three commits pushed to main (and now live on Vercel):

  ---
  Commit 1 — 39c959e Pivot to Tally + result page stub

  The big architectural shift. Abandoned the custom-coded 10-question UI in
  favor of a hosted Tally form.

  Deleted (~2,500 lines):
  - app/questionnaire/[step]/, app/questionnaire/layout.tsx
  - components/questions/ — all 9 question components (Piece, Seed,
  ReferenceShelf, Teachers, Ghost, AIHelpers, AIGenerator, PositionDot,
  Collaborators)
  - components/shared/StepNav.tsx, MultiSelectCard.tsx
  - lib/context.tsx, lib/steps.ts, lib/hooks/useRovingTabIndex.ts

  Added:
  - app/questionnaire/page.tsx — full-viewport Tally iframe + next/script loader
   for tally.so/widgets/embed.js
  - app/result/page.tsx — client component reading useSearchParams, with a
  parseTallyParams() stub returning {} and a dev-only debug block showing raw
  URL params

  Schema changes (lib/schema.ts):
  - Q3 references: dropped position; weight is now literal union 0.2 | 0.5 | 
  0.85
  - Q6 aiHelpers: removed 'none'; empty array signals no helpers
  - Q8 directionExecution: integer 1–10 instead of {x, y}
  - Q9 collaborators: removed 'just-me'; empty array signals just me
  - Q10 feltOwnership: integer 1–10
  - aiHelpers and collaborators now use .array(...) (no .min(1))

  Other:
  - app/api/grace/route.ts — kept as stub but now imports ProvenanceResponse to
  stay schema-aware
  - app/page.tsx — removed "your answers stay on your device" line
  - Docs: changelog.md (Session 12), requirements.md (Core Flow rewritten +
  per-Q updates), bugs.md ("Resolved by removal" section), backlog.md (V2 entry
  to re-implement reflective UI), CLAUDE.md (file structure, schema-at-a-glance,
   new "Tally integration" section, anti-patterns)

  ---
  Commit 2 — 7d30a40 Rename to Creative Trace

  Project name change after securing the creativetrace.art domain. The old
  creative-provenance.vercel.app URL is kept in docs everywhere as a documented
  redirect (handled at the Vercel/DNS level).

  Code:
  - package.json name → creative-trace
  - app/layout.tsx metadata.title → Creative Trace
  - app/page.tsx heading → Creative Trace
  - app/questionnaire/page.tsx iframe title → Creative Trace
  - lib/storage.ts localStorage key → creative-trace-response

  Docs:
  - README.md (title, project structure refreshed for post-pivot, dual-URL
  deployment block)
  - CLAUDE.md (project description × 2, deployment URL × 2)
  - docs/requirements.md (header, share-payload title, PNG filename pattern,
  symposium URL block)
  - docs/questionnaire-draft.md (header)
  - docs/backlog.md ("Custom domain" item struck through with redirect note)
  - docs/changelog.md (Session 12.1 entry)

  Intentionally NOT renamed: past changelog entries, docs/opening-prompt.md, the
   Tally form's title (edited in Tally), the repo directory name.

  ---
  Commit 3 — a206423 Tally REST fetch via /result?sid={submissionId}

  Tally now redirects to /result?sid={submissionId}. The result page fetches the
   full submission server-side instead of trying to read every answer from URL
  params.

  New:
  - lib/tally.ts:
    - fetchSubmission(sid) — GET 
  https://api.tally.so/forms/RGZO7p/submissions/{sid} with Authorization: Bearer
   ${TALLY_API_KEY}. 404s flag .status for the API route to relay.
    - First successful call per process logs the raw response shape so we can
  inspect and refine the mapping.
    - mapTallyToProvenance() — best-effort label/key substring matching;
  resolves option IDs to text via the field's options table; matches against the
   schema's literal unions; clamps numeric scales to 1–10. TODO comments mark Q3
   per-tile bucket fields and Q7 branch presence as needing real-submission
  confirmation.
  - app/api/tally-submission/route.ts — GET handler. 400 on missing sid, 404 on
  submission not found, 500 on other errors.

  Modified:
  - app/result/page.tsx — removed parseTallyParams. Reads sid only, fetches on
  mount, renders loading/error/ok states. Adds strip and Grace placeholder
  sections. Dev-only debug block now shows sid + mapped ProvenanceResponse.
  Initial state is derived from sid presence (avoids React 19's
  set-state-in-effect lint rule).
  - .env.example and .env.local — added TALLY_API_KEY placeholder.
  - docs/changelog.md — Session 13 entry.

  ---
  What's now live and what's still stubbed

  Live:
  - Tally embed at /questionnaire works end-to-end
  - /result?sid=... will fetch and display the mapped response (once you fill in
   TALLY_API_KEY and configure Tally's redirect)
  - Production at creativetrace.art (with creative-provenance.vercel.app
  redirecting to it)

  Still stubbed:
  - The strip area (visual system pending from Paola/Yash)
  - The Grace text area (/api/grace still returns { grace: '' })
  - parseTallyParams was deleted; mapTallyToProvenance is best-effort and needs
  refinement after one real submission is logged

  What you need to do next:
  1. Fill in TALLY_API_KEY in .env.local and add it to Vercel's environment
  variables (all three environments)
  2. Configure Tally to redirect to /result?sid={submissionId} on submit
  3. Submit one real form, check the server console for the logged raw shape,
  refine the heuristics in mapTallyToProvenance against the actual field
  labels/keys
  4. Visual system + Grace generation come after that

  lib/tally.ts rewritten:
  - QUESTION_IDS lookup keyed by the 15 form question UUIDs you provided
  - 8 TEXT_TO_SCHEMA constants with the exact Tally option text → schema literal
   (medium, seed, teacher, aiHelper, aiKind, aiStage, aiAwareness, collaborator)
  - null values mark intentional opt-outs ("None of these", "Nobody — just me")
  that resolve to empty arrays
  - Unmapped text emits console.warn and is skipped
  - Q3 references mapped from the 12 matrix row UUIDs to ReferenceTileId; bucket
   text (Barely/A little/A lot) → weight (0.2/0.5/0.85); only rows the user
  selected are included
  - Q7 gate: aiUsed === ["Yes"] populates branch fields; ["No"] produces
  aiGenerator = { used: false } with branch fields omitted
  - Removed the "first submission" log + loggedRawShapeOnce from
  fetchSubmission; left the rest of fetchSubmission intact
  - Removed all the heuristic helpers (findField, resolveChoices, matchSlug,
  bucketFromLabel)

  Other:
  - CLAUDE.md Tally integration + prioritization sections updated to describe
  the REST fetch + UUID-pinned mapping (no more parseTallyParams references)
  - docs/changelog.md Session 13.1 entry added

  Decisions you should review:

  1. References use the schema's ReferenceTileId enum, not the friendly IDs from
   your prompt. Your prompt described the matrix mapping as id: "artists", id: 
  "curated", etc., with id: string. The schema's ReferenceTileId is a strict
  enum ('artist-portfolios', 'curated-channels', etc.) and you said don't touch
  the schema, so I mapped the matrix UUIDs directly to those enum values. Tell
  me if you actually wanted the friendly IDs and we'll swap (will require schema
   changes).
  2. Ownership uses why, not ownershipWhy. Your prompt described the schema
  field as ownershipWhy?: string but the actual field in lib/schema.ts is why.
  Used why.
  3. Option text is taken from docs/questionnaire-draft.md. I assumed the Tally
  form's option strings exactly match the questionnaire draft (including
  punctuation: em-dashes, smart quotes, '/'/"/"). If Tally normalized any of
  those during form creation (a common gotcha — Tally sometimes converts
  quotes), unmapped options will show up as console.warn lines. First real
  submission will surface any mismatches; fix them by editing the relevant
  TEXT_TO_SCHEMA key.
  4. Rebased on top of a Vercel Web Analytics PR (commit ed5598a) that landed
  remotely while I was working. No conflicts; rebase was clean. The Analytics
  component now sits in app/layout.tsx and the @vercel/analytics package is in
  deps — that's existing remote work, not my doing.
  5. Q2 seed is single-select, schema is array. Your prompt said "take first
  element"; schema requires seed.types: SeedType[]. I take the first element,
  map it, and wrap as a single-element array [mappedSeed]. If a user picks
  "Other" in Tally with a fill-in text, that text isn't currently captured (no
  questionId provided for it).

⏺ Pushed as 104d69a.

  Summary

  Root cause: Your diagnosis pointed at QUESTION_IDS but that table was already
  keyed by the short Tally IDs (NVk1pG, qB6142, …) — verified by re-reading the
  file. The actual bug was one level deeper: the response items hold the answer
  payload under value in some Tally REST shapes, but findAnswer only read
  .answer. Every lookup returned undefined, so every mapped field collapsed to
  its schema default — exactly the "empty/default values" symptom you described.

  Fix in lib/tally.ts:
  - TallyResponseItem now declares both answer?: unknown and value?: unknown.
  - findAnswer prefers answer and falls back to value.
  - New extractResponses(submission) also accepts the wrapped shape
  submission.submissions[0].responses (some Tally endpoints nest a single
  submission under submissions[0]).
  - console.warn when no responses are extracted, listing the submission's
  top-level keys — so any future shape drift is immediately visible in logs.

  Verification hook: app/api/tally-submission/route.ts now logs [tally] 
  sid=X54L4bg mapped: {...} on every request. After the deploy lands, hit
  /result?sid=X54L4bg (or just /api/tally-submission?sid=X54L4bg) and check
  Vercel function logs — you should see:
  - piece.description: "Test"
  - piece.medium: "fiber"
  - ghost: { present: true, description: "My toxic ex" }
  - directionExecution: 7
  - ownership: { feltOwnership: 7, … }

  If anything is still empty, the log will tell us exactly what's missing —
  either an unrecognized response shape (the warn fires) or an option-text
  mismatch (the per-question unmapped X option: warn fires from Session 13.1's
  mapOne/mapMany helpers).

  Things to flag once verified:
  - I couldn't run the API call locally to actually confirm — verification
  requires your TALLY_API_KEY. If the empty-fields symptom persists after the
  deploy, the next-most-likely cause is option-text drift (e.g. Tally normalized
   a smart quote or em-dash). Send me a [tally] unmapped X option: "..." line
  from your logs and I'll patch the matching TEXT_TO_SCHEMA key.
  - The console.log in the API route is intentional for now — leave it through
  symposium prep so we have a record of what mapped successfully. Easy to gate
  behind process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production' later if you want to silence it
  in prod.

⏺ Pushed as 1a4b492.

  Summary

  You were right — this was the actual bug. Tally's single-submission endpoint
  returns:

  { questions: [...], submission: { id: "X54L4bg", responses: [...] } }

  The mapper's parameter was named submission but it was really the envelope.
  extractResponses checked env.responses and env.submissions[0].responses but
  never env.submission.responses, so every findAnswer call ran against an empty
  array — exactly why every field came back as its schema default.

  Fix:
  - Split the type: TallyInnerSubmission (the real submission) vs.
  TallySubmission (the envelope, with the inner submission field plus tolerated
  alternates)
  - extractInnerSubmission(env) now reads env.submission.responses first, then
  falls back to env.responses, then env.submissions[0]
  - Metadata (id, submittedAt) is now also read from the inner submission

  Temporary diagnostic logging at the top of mapTallyToProvenance (tagged
  "temporary; remove once mapping is stable"):

  1. [tally] envelope top-level keys: ['questions', 'submission']
  2. [tally] envelope.submission exists: true
  3. [tally] envelope.submission.responses exists: true length: N
  4. [tally] first 3 responses: [{questionId, answer}, ...]
  5. [tally] QUESTION_IDS keys: ['piece', 'medium', ...]

  To verify: hit /result?sid=X54L4bg (or /api/tally-submission?sid=X54L4bg) and
  check Vercel function logs. You should see those five [tally] ... lines, then
  the existing [tally] sid=X54L4bg mapped: {...} line should now contain
  piece.description: "Test", medium: "fiber", ghost.description: "My toxic ex",
  directionExecution: 7, ownership.feltOwnership: 7.

  If anything is still empty after this, the diagnostic logs will pinpoint why —
   either an unrecognized envelope shape (logs 1–3 won't match) or an
  option-text mismatch (a [tally] unmapped X option: warn will fire).

  Once you've confirmed it works on a real submission, ask me to remove the
  diagnostic block.

  app/api/grace/route.ts.                                                       
                                                                                
  Context: Grace is an AI-generated reflective text shown on the /result page   
  after                                                                         
  the form submission. It reads like a Catholic grace prayer — a moment to name 
   what                                                                         
  was given to you. It draws from every answer in the submission and ends with  
  the                                                                           
  felt-ownership score, holding the tension between what the respondent feels   
  and                                                                           
  what actually went into the piece.                                            
                                                                                
  IMPORTANT: Q10 (feltOwnership) is about what the user FEELS about the work,   
  not                                                                           
  what it is. The grace should surface this tension — the felt ownership may    
  contradict the inputs. This is why ownership isn't in the visual signature.   
                                                                                
  1. Implement app/api/grace/route.ts:                                          
     - POST handler, accepts { submission: Partial<ProvenanceResponse> } body   
     - Calls Anthropic API (https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages) with:        
       - model: "claude-sonnet-4-6-20250514"                                    
       - max_tokens: 500                                                        
       - Authorization: Bearer ${process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}                 
       - anthropic-version: "2023-06-01"                                        
     - System prompt (see below)                                                
     - Returns { grace: string }                                                
     - 400 if no submission, 500 on API error                                   
                                                                                
  2. System prompt for Grace generation:                                        
                                                                                
  """                                                                           
  You write graces. A grace is a prayer said before a meal — a moment to pause  
  and name what was given to you before you take the first bite.                
                                                                                
  You will receive a JSON object describing a creative work and everything that 
                                                                                
  fed it: what the piece is, how it began, what the maker soaked in, who taught 
                                                                                
  them, whether a ghost haunts it, what AI tools were involved, who else shaped 
                                                                                
  it, and how much ownership the maker feels.                                   
                                                                                
  Write a grace for this piece. Rules:                                          
                                                                                
  - Each line begins with "Thank you to..." or "Thank you for..."               
  - One line per distinct contribution source. Be specific — use the actual     
    details from the submission, not generic placeholders.                      
  - If there's a ghost (ghost.present=true), name it using ghost.description.   
    Keep the maker's words.                                                     
  - If AI was used (aiGenerator.used=true), acknowledge both the tool and the   
    training data tension (aiAwareness field).                                  
  - If collaborators are present, thank them.                                   
  - The last two lines are always about felt ownership. Format:                 
    "You feel this piece is [natural language of feltOwnership score 1-10]."    
    "Sit with that."                                                            
                                                                                
    feltOwnership mapping:                                                      
    1-2: "not really yours"                                                     
    3-4: "only partly yours"                                                    
    5-6: "half yours"                                                           
    7-8: "almost entirely yours"                                                
    9-10: "completely yours"                                                    
                                                                                
  - Keep it short: 5-9 "thank you" lines plus the ownership closing.            
  - No preamble, no sign-off, no explanation. Just the grace.                   
  - Each line should be on its own line.                                        
  - Do not use the word "Amen."                                                 
  - Tone: warm, direct, unflinching. Mirror, don't judge.

  Decisions you should review:

  1. Auth header is x-api-key, not Authorization: Bearer. Your spec said Bearer,
   but sk-ant-… keys are direct API keys — the canonical Anthropic header is
  x-api-key. Bearer would 401. Worth knowing if you're copying the pattern
  elsewhere.
  2. System prompt is inlined in the route file, not in lib/grace-prompt.ts
  (which is still empty from the original scaffold). Inlining keeps the single
  source of truth next to the call site for now; happy to extract later when
  iteration picks up.
  3. System prompt says "aiAwareness field" but the schema field is 
  aiGenerator.trainingDataAwareness. I kept your prompt verbatim. The model
  should figure it out from the JSON context, but if graces ever miss the
  training-data tension on AI-used submissions, that's the first place I'd
  tighten the wording.
  4. No rate limiting yet. /api/grace is currently unguarded — anyone with the
  URL can burn API credits. Symposium prep should add a per-IP rate limit
  (in-memory Map or Vercel KV). Logged in CLAUDE.md "What to Prioritize."
  5. Grace state derives "loading" from outer state, not its own enum. React
  19's set-state-in-effect rule blocks the obvious setGraceState({ status: 
  'loading' }) inside the effect. I removed 'loading' from the GraceState union
  and compute graceLoading = state.status === 'ok' && graceState.status === 
  'idle' in render. Equivalent UX, lint-clean.
  6. Used claude-sonnet-4-6 alias per your follow-up. Updated in route.ts,
  CLAUDE.md, and changelog.

⏺ Pushed as ebf097b.

  Summary

  1. localStorage cache (the important one):
  - New helpers readCachedGrace(sid) / writeCachedGrace(sid, grace) in
  app/result/page.tsx. SSR-safe (typeof window guard); silent-fail if
  localStorage is disabled (private browsing).
  - graceState's useState initializer reads the cache — on revisit the grace
  appears instantly with no API call and no loading flash.
  - The fetch effect re-checks the cache and bails out before hitting /api/grace
   if an entry exists. After a successful generation, the grace is written back.
   Same sid → same answers → same grace, so Anthropic is only called once per 
  submission.

  2. Bold the subjects:
  - Added the new rule to SYSTEM_PROMPT in app/api/grace/route.ts, with the
  verbatim example you provided ("Thank you to your toxic ex, …").
  - renderGraceLine(line) in app/result/page.tsx splits each line on **…**
  matches and renders the captured text as <strong>; everything else renders as
  plain text. Regex-based, no markdown library. Lines without bold spans render
  unchanged.
  - <GraceLines> now calls renderGraceLine per paragraph; italic styling on the
  parent is unchanged, so <strong> shows as bold-italic.

  3. Changelog Session 14.1 entry added with the full description.

  Things to flag:

  1. Hydration safety — the useState initializer reads localStorage only when
  typeof window !== 'undefined'. The <Suspense fallback={null}> boundary above
  ResultContent means the inner component renders client-only (because
  useSearchParams suspends during SSR), so the initializer never runs on the
  server. No hydration mismatch.
  2. Cache invalidation is sid-keyed, which is the right call — submissions are
  immutable in Tally (you can't edit a submitted form). If you ever do need to
  bust caches (e.g. after editing the Grace prompt), bumping the cache key
  prefix to grace-v2-${sid} is a one-line change. Mention if you want me to add
  that lever pre-emptively.
  3. Bold parser is intentionally minimal — it only handles **bold**.
  Single-asterisk italics, escaped asterisks, nested formatting, and any other
  markdown all pass through as literal text. Matches the system prompt, which
  only asks for bold. If Claude ever decides to slip in a _underscore_ or # 
  heading, it'll render literally; that's a feature, not a bug.
  4. Existing graces in users' localStorage from before this session won't have
  the bold formatting — they'll render as plain italic. If you want every old
  grace re-generated, bump the cache key (see #2). I'd suggest leaving it: the
  next genuine new submission will pick up the bold formatting, and old graces
  are still valid text.

  literals. Per your "use the schema's version" instruction, I used these
  instead:

  ┌──────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │     Map      │                     You said → I used                     │

  ├──────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤

  │              │ ai-teacher                                                │
  ├──────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │              │ color-correction → auto-correction; reference-search →    │
  │ AI Helper    │ search; spell-check → autosuggest; voice-to-text →        │
  │              │ transcription; generative-suggestions → recommendations   │
  ├──────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ AI Kind      │ animation → motion                                        │
  ├──────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤

  │              │ kept-as-is → mostly-as-is; whole-piece → all-ai           │

  │              │ artists-like-me; can-name → specific-artists              │
  ├──────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ Collaborator │ photographer → commissioned-creator                       │
  └──────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  No options needed to be skipped — every option in your list had a
  corresponding schema literal.

  Variants added per your rules:
  - Em dash (—) keys with " - " hyphen-with-spaces siblings: An image that stuck
   — … and The whole piece — I shaped it from AI output
  - Apostrophe (') keys with curly (') siblings: wouldn't, can't, didn't,
  Haven't, couldn't
  - Bonus: kept a curly-double-quote variant of Reference search (Google Images,
   visual search, "find similar") so the "find similar" smart-quoting also
  matches

  Notes for review:

  1. No "None of these" (Q6) or "Nobody — just me" (Q9) in your live-form list.
  I removed them from the maps. The schema's empty-array convention still covers
   both cases — if a respondent picks nothing, the resulting empty array signals
   "no helpers" / "just me" exactly as before. If those options are still in the
   form and you simply didn't paste them, they'll log as [tally] unmapped 
  aiHelper option: / unmapped collaborator option: warns and be skipped (which
  gives the correct empty-array semantics anyway, just noisier logs).
  2. Something else... for medium uses three ASCII periods. If Tally renders a
  real ellipsis (… U+2026) it'll log as unmapped — let me know and I'll add the
  variant.
  3. Q4 collaborator "The model, the performer..." is the only "The …" key in
  collaborators while everything else is "A …". Kept verbatim per your list, but
   flag in case it's actually "A model, …" in the form.
  4. Temporary debug logging (the diagnostic block + per-item raw dump) was
  already removed in the prior commit 2d45532 before this edit — file is clean
  of those. The unmapped-option console.warn calls in mapMany/mapOne and the
  final mapped-output console.log in app/api/tally-submission/route.ts remain.

❯ Read app/api/grace/route.ts.                                                  
                                                                                
  Update the system prompt: the grace should be written in first person         
  (I/me/my),                                                                    
  not second person (you/your). A grace is spoken by the person sitting down to 
   eat,                                                                         
  not narrated at them.                                                         
                                                                                
  Example — current: "Thank you to your toxic ex, whose presence in this work

  Summary

  System prompt updated:

  - New top-of-rules clause: "First person only. The grace is the maker's own
  voice — I/me/my, never you/your. It is spoken by the person sitting down to
  look at the work, not narrated at them."
  - Bold example: your toxic ex / you neither invited → my toxic ex / I neither 
  invited
  - Closing template: "You feel this piece is …." / "Sit with that." → "I feel 
  this piece is …." / "Let me sit with that."
  - feltOwnership mapping flipped to mine forms: not really mine / only partly 
  mine / half mine / almost entirely mine / completely mine

  Things to flag

  1. Prompt-cache invalidation — Anthropic's ephemeral cache is keyed on the
  exact system-prompt bytes, so this edit silently busts the cache. The first
  request after the deploy lands will miss the cache and refresh it; subsequent
  requests pay the cheap rate again. No action needed.
  2. Existing per-sid localStorage graces still render in the old voice. Users
  who already received a grace will see their old you/your version cached on
  their device. Two options:
    - Leave it — old graces are still valid; only new submissions get the
  first-person voice.
    - Bump the cache key prefix from grace-${sid} to grace-v2-${sid} in
  app/result/page.tsx to force a refresh for every previously-cached user.

  Tell me if you want option 2 and I'll make the one-line change.
  3. Ghost rule still says "Keep the maker's words" — that's an instruction to
  Claude (preserve the maker's exact phrasing for the ghost description), not a
  voice issue. Left as-is.
  4. GraceLines rendering still works unchanged. Two ownership lines,
  second-to-last gets pt-6 for the visual step. "I feel this piece is …" / "Let
  me sit with that." occupies the same two-line slot.

      12 +                                                               
      13  ## Session 14.1 -- 2026-04-29 -- Cache the grace + bold the sub
          jects
      14  - **Client-side grace cache.** `/result?sid=X` now stores gener
          ated graces in `localStorage` under the key `grace-${sid}`. On 
          page load, the initializer reads the cache and pre-populates `g
          raceState` so the grace appears instantly on revisit. The fetch
           effect re-checks the cache and bails out before hitting `/api/
          grace` if a cached entry exists. After a successful generation,
           the new grace is written back to the cache. Same `sid` → same 
          answers → same grace, so we only ever pay Anthropic once per su
          bmission. Stops spending API credits on every refresh and gives
           users a stable text.
      15  - The cache reader/writer is SSR-safe (typeof window guard) and
           tolerates `localStorage` being disabled (private browsing) — s
          ilent fail, falls through to a fresh fetch.

❯ Read CLAUDE.md, lib/schema.ts, and app/result/page.tsx.                       
                                                                                
  Context: Build the Tracemark — a generative 18×18 unit SVG grid that          
  visualizes a Creative Trace submission. Each unit = 30px, so the full         
  grid renders at 540×540px. The grid has 9 patches, each driven by             
  different question data. Render as a React component.                         
                                                                                
  Create components/Tracemark.tsx:                                              
                                                                                
  GRID SYSTEM:                                                                  
  - viewBox="0 0 540 540" (18 units × 30px each)                                
  - Black (#000000) stroke on all patch boundaries, 2px weight                  
  - Three rows, each 180px (6 units) tall                                       
  - Component accepts: { data: Partial<ProvenanceResponse>, size?: number }

  Summary

  components/Tracemark.tsx — generative 540×540 SVG grid (1 unit = 30px). All
  nine patches built per spec:

  ┌─────┬─────────┬────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  #  │  Size   │       Driver       │                Notes                │
  ├─────┼─────────┼────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 0   │ 60×180  │ static             │ solid #000 anchor                   │
  ├─────┼─────────┼────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
  │     │         │                    │ MEDIUM_COLOR map; fallback #B5DD35. │
  │ 1   │ 180×180 │ piece.medium       │  TODO comment for the seed-pattern  │
  │     │         │                    │ overlay                             │
  ├─────┼─────────┼────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 3   │ 300×180 │ references[]       │ 5 vertical sections; fill height =  │
  │     │         │                    │ avg weight × 180                    │
  ├─────┼─────────┼────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 4   │ 240×180 │ teachers[]         │ 8 cells; spec's "crit" → schema's   │
  │     │         │                    │ 'critique'                          │
  ├─────┼─────────┼────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 5   │ 210×180 │ aiGenerator.used   │ base #8CBBA1; bottom-right #567550  │
  │     │         │                    │ triangle when used === false        │
  ├─────┼─────────┼────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 6   │ 90×180  │ aiHelpers[]        │ 12-slot grid (30×45); 12th slot is  │
  │     │         │                    │ always base color                   │
  ├─────┼─────────┼────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
  │     │         │                    │ 16-cell grid mixing kinds + stage + │
  │ 7   │ 180×180 │ aiGenerator        │  awareness via discriminated union; │
  │     │         │                    │  flat fill if used !== true         │
  ├─────┼─────────┼────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 8   │ 180×180 │ directionExecution │ bar Math.ceil(value/2) cols capped  │
  │     │         │                    │ at 6; 5 internal column dividers    │
  ├─────┼─────────┼────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ 9   │ 180×180 │ collaborators[]    │ same row pattern as Patch 4; last   │
  │     │         │                    │ row always base                     │
  └─────┴─────────┴────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────┘

  Each patch is a <g transform="translate(x,y)"> group. A PatchBorder (2px #000
  fill="none" rect) draws last per patch — adjacent patches each draw their own
  border, the strokes overlap perfectly, and the result is a clean 2px line on
  every shared edge. shapeRendering="crispEdges" on the root SVG keeps the grid
  alignment pixel-perfect at small sizes.

  Props: { data: Partial<ProvenanceResponse>; size?: number; className?: string 
  }. size sets width/height attributes (default 540); viewBox is locked to 0 0 
  540 540. className flows through so the caller can scale (h-auto w-full 
  max-w-[540px] for responsive).

  app/result/page.tsx — replaced the placeholder card with the Tracemark when
  state.status === 'ok'. During the fetch, a dashed-border placeholder shows
  "Tracemark — loading…". Wrapped in <section className="flex justify-center">
  so the 540px Tracemark sits centered within the 700px page column.

  Things to flag

  1. Patch 8 dividers — spec said "6 vertical divider lines" but 6 columns only
  have 5 internal boundaries. I drew 5 internal <line>s plus the 2px patch
  border on the outer edges. Net visual effect: 6 columns clearly delineated. If
   you wanted 6 internal lines (i.e., one column has no leading divider, or one
  line overlaps the patch border), tell me and I'll switch.
  2. Patch border overlap — adjacent patches each draw a 2px stroke at their
  shared edge, so the strokes overlap and the line stays 2px instead of doubling
   to 4px. Outer grid edges only get one stroke (1px inside, 1px outside the
  540×540 viewBox). On the rendered HTML page that means the outer edge looks
  like a 1px line; if you want a 2px outer edge too, easy fix is to inset the
  patch borders by 1px or render an extra outer rect.
  3. Patch 1 pattern overlay — left as a TODO comment in the source. When
  Paola/Yash deliver the seed-type pattern assets, they slot in as an <image> or
   <pattern> overlay on top of the medium-colored base inside Patch 1.
  4. Empty-data rendering — if data is {} or only partially populated, the
  Tracemark still renders. Patches show base colors with no selections; Patch 1
  falls back to the other color (#B5DD35); Patch 5 fills #8CBBA1 and shows the
  "AI-not-used" triangle (since aiUsed defaults to false); Patch 8's bar has
  zero width. So the Tracemark works as a graceful fallback for the loading
  state if you ever want to show it pre-fetch.
  5. Small mobile layout — max-w-[540px] plus w-full makes the Tracemark scale
  down on narrow viewports. The 30px units become smaller proportionally;
  readability of subdivisions stays intact down to ~360px wide. Below that, the
  grid still renders, just gets denser.

⏺ Pushed as 5d75f99.

  Summary

  1. Stroke width — proportional to grid unit
  - const UNIT = 30; const STROKE_WIDTH = UNIT / 6; (= 5px)
  - Used everywhere: cell strokes, patch borders, P5 diagonal, P8 column
  dividers, outer border. No hardcoded widths anywhere.

  2. Rendering order — fill/stroke split
  - Added two helpers, FillRects and StrokeRects, that take the same cells array
   and render two passes (fills first with no stroke, then stroke-only rects on
  top with no fill).
  - Patches 4, 6, 7, 9 use the helpers. Patch 3 uses three explicit passes
  (base, bars, stroke outlines). Patch 5 uses polygons + diagonal-on-top. Patch
  8 background → bar → dividers → border. Patch border is the final element in
  every patch.
  - Net result: no fill can ever paint over a stroke.

  3. Patch 5 — always draw the diagonal
  - Two polygons drawn unconditionally: upper-left (0,0)-(210,0)-(0,180),
  lower-right (210,0)-(210,180)-(0,180).
  - aiUsed === true → upper-left fill #567550 (dark), lower-right fill #8CBBA1
  (light).
  - aiUsed === false/undefined → both halves #8CBBA1.
  - Diagonal <line> from (210,0) → (0,180) drawn last, always.

  4. Patch 7 — grid always renders
  - Removed the flat-fill fallback. The 16-cell grid renders unconditionally.
  - When used !== true, all 16 cells use base #E98FC6 (none selected) but the
  strokes still draw, so the grid structure remains visible.
  - Cell sizes verified: rows 1–4 are 60×30, rows 5–6 are 90×30. The awareness
  cells in rows 5–6 are 1.5× the width of the kinds/stage cells above them.

  5. Patch 8 — dividers on top of bar
  - Order: background → bar → 5 column dividers → patch border. Dividers now sit
   on top of the bar fill at 5px stroke.

  6. Color audit
  All 23 hex codes extracted into named constants (MEDIUM_COLOR.*, PATCH3_BASE,
  PATCH3_FILL, … PATCH9_SELECTED) and verified against the spec — every one
  matches. Full audit table is in the commit message.

  7. Outer border
  Single 540×540 fill="none" stroke="#000" strokeWidth={5} rect, rendered last.

  Note about the outer border at 5px width: half the stroke (2.5px) lies at the
  boundary of the viewBox. SVG default behavior clips at the viewBox edge, so
  visually the outer border may render as ~2.5px on the outside-facing half,
  while internal grid lines render as the full 5px. If you want the outer edge
  to look identical in weight to the internal lines, the standard fix is to
  inset that final rect by half the stroke (i.e. x={2.5} y={2.5} width={535} 
  height={535}). Tell me if you want that change.

       98 +async function downloadTracemarkPNG(                          
       99 +  wrapper: HTMLElement,                                       
      100 +  sid: string,                                                
      101 +): Promise<void> {                                            
      102 +  const svg = wrapper.querySelector('svg');                   
      103 +  if (!svg) return;                                           
      104 +                                                              
      105 +  // Clone so we don't mutate what's on screen, and ensure xml
          +ns is present                                                 
      106 +  // for standalone serialization.                            
      107 +  const cloned = svg.cloneNode(true) as SVGSVGElement;        
      108 +  if (!cloned.getAttribute('xmlns')) {                        
      109 +    cloned.setAttribute('xmlns', 'http://www.w3.org/2000/svg')
          +;                                                             
      110 +  }                                                           
      111 +  const svgString = new XMLSerializer().serializeToString(clon
          +ed);                                                          
      112 +  const svgBlob = new Blob([svgString], {                     
      113 +    type: 'image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8',                      
      114 +  });                                                         
      115 +  const svgUrl = URL.createObjectURL(svgBlob);                
      116 +                                                              
      117 +  try {                                                       
      118 +    const img = new Image();                                  
      119 +    await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {            
      120 +      img.onload = () => resolve();                           
      121 +      img.onerror = () => reject(new Error('Failed to load SVG
          +'));                                                          
      122 +      img.src = svgUrl;                                       
      123 +    });                                                       
      124 +                                                              
      125 +    const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');          
      126 +    canvas.width = 1080;                                      
      127 +    canvas.height = 1080;                                     
      128 +    const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');                      
      129 +    if (!ctx) return;                                         
      130 +    ctx.fillStyle = '#ffffff';                                
      131 +    ctx.fillRect(0, 0, 1080, 1080);                           
      132 +    ctx.drawImage(img, 0, 0, 1080, 1080);                     
      133 +                                                              
      134 +    const blob = await new Promise<Blob | null>((resolve) => {
      135 +      canvas.toBlob(resolve, 'image/png');                    
      136 +    });                                                       
      137 +    if (!blob) return;                                        
      138 +                                                              
      139 +    const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);                    
      140 +    const a = document.createElement('a');                    
      141 +    a.href = url;                                             
      142 +    a.download = `tracemark-${sid}.png`;                      
      143 +    document.body.appendChild(a);                             
      144 +    a.click();                                                
      145 +    document.body.removeChild(a);                             
      146 +    URL.revokeObjectURL(url);                                 
      147 +  } finally {                                                 
      148 +    URL.revokeObjectURL(svgUrl);                              
      149 +  }

       1  # Changelog
       2  
       3 +## Session 17 -- 2026-04-29 -- Symposium UX polish: hero, two-c
         +ol result, download/share, grace styling                       
       4 +- **Landing hero**: added `HeroGrid` above the title — six hard
         +coded sample `Partial<ProvenanceResponse>` objects rendered as 
         +120px Tracemarks in a 3×2 grid. Each sample is deliberately dis
         +tinct (different mediums, teacher mixes, AI used or not, varyin
         +g ownership scores) so the marks read as a visual sample rather
         + than near-duplicates. Tilted via per-cell rotation/translate-y
         + transforms (`-rotate-3`, `rotate-2 translate-y-2`, etc.) for a
         + "stickers laid on a surface" look. Marked `aria-hidden` so scr
         +een readers skip the decorative grid.                          
       5 +- **CTA color**: landing CTA button background changed from `bg
         +-black` to `bg-[#3E51C0]` (deep blue from the palette). White t
         +ext preserved. The download button on the result page picks up 
         +the same color; the share button uses an outlined variant (`bor
         +der-[#3E51C0]` + transparent fill + blue text).                
       6 +- **Result page two-column layout**: at `md+`, the page becomes
         + a grid (`md:grid md:grid-cols-[minmax(0,440px)_1fr] md:gap-12`
         +). Left column holds the Tracemark (`max-w-[440px]`) plus the a
         +ction buttons, and uses `md:sticky md:top-8 md:self-start` so i
         +t stays in view while the user scrolls the grace. Mobile keeps 
         +the existing single-column stack. Page max-width bumped from `7
         +00px` to `1000px` to accommodate the side-by-side layout.      
       7 +- **Download Tracemark**: new button below the Tracemark. Click
         + handler clones the live SVG, serializes it, draws it on an off

⏺ Pushed as 782d26f.

  Summary

  1. Landing hero grid — HeroGrid component above the title with six hardcoded
  sample Partial<ProvenanceResponse> objects rendered as 120px Tracemarks in a
  3×2 grid. Each sample is distinct
  (painted/digital-2d/3d-digital/printed/fiber/mixed-media; different teacher
  mixes; AI used/not; varied ownership scores). Per-cell rotate/translate-y
  transforms (-rotate-3, rotate-2 translate-y-2, etc.) for a
  stickers-on-a-surface feel. aria-hidden since it's decorative.

  2. Result page two-column layout — md:grid md:grid-cols-[minmax(0,440px)_1fr] 
  md:gap-12. Left = Tracemark + buttons, sticky via md:sticky md:top-8 
  md:self-start. Right = grace intro + grace box. Mobile stacks. Page max-width
  bumped 700 → 1000. Removed the "How is your data used?" section entirely
  (duplicate of landing footnote).

  3. Download Tracemark — Button below the Tracemark. Clones the live SVG,
  serializes via XMLSerializer, loads as Image from a URL.createObjectURL blob,
  draws on an offscreen 1080×1080 canvas (white bg), and triggers
  tracemark-${sid}.png via canvas.toBlob. All Object URLs revoked in finally.

  4. Share button — Outlined variant. Tries navigator.share({ title, text, url 
  }); falls back to navigator.clipboard.writeText(url) with a "Link copied!"
  toast (fixed bottom-center pill, auto-dismiss 2s).

  5. Grace mobile sizing — text-sm md:text-base on lines, space-y-1.5 
  md:space-y-2, ownership-line pt-5 md:pt-6, container p-4 md:p-6. Intro stays
  small.

  6. Grace box styling — Removed the rounded all-around border. New treatment:
  3px left accent border-l-[3px] border-[#3E51C0] + warm off-white background
  bg-[#F8F7F6]. Italic and bold subjects preserved.

  7. CTA color — Landing CTA bg-black → bg-[#3E51C0]. The result page Download
  button matches; Share is the outlined variant of the same.

  8. Changelog — Session 17 entry added.

  Things to flag

  1. Sticky behavior on the result page — md:sticky + md:self-start keeps the
  Tracemark column visible while the grace scrolls. If the grace is short enough
   to fit one viewport with the Tracemark, sticky has no effect (nothing to
  scroll). Real submissions should produce 5–9 thank-you lines plus closing,
  which on a 720px viewport will exceed the Tracemark's height — sticky kicks in
   there.
  2. Download CORS / tainted-canvas risk — The Tracemark SVG has no external
  resources (no <image>, no remote fonts), so canvas.toBlob won't trigger a CORS
   taint. Confirmed safe with the current Tracemark structure. If the visual
  system later adds external pattern overlays, the canvas approach may need
  img.crossOrigin = 'anonymous' plus CORS-enabled hosts.
  3. navigator.share browser support — Available on iOS Safari, modern Android,
  and most desktop Chromes (with files only on mobile). The fallback (clipboard)
   is universally available. Toast appears on both paths if needed.
  4. Hero strokes at 120px — STROKE_WIDTH in viewBox is 5px; at size=120 those
  become ~1.1px on screen. Strokes will be thin on the small marks. Looks
  intentional/graphic at small scale, but if the user wants them chunkier, the
  only lever is to bump STROKE_WIDTH in Tracemark.tsx (which would also affect
  the result page render). Flagging because spec said don't touch Tracemark.tsx
  — happy to revisit if needed.
  5. 6 vs 8 hero marks — Spec said "6–8 sample Tracemarks". I went with 6 in a
  clean 3×2 grid. Easy to extend to 8 in a 4×2 grid by adding two more samples
  to the array if needed.
  6. Toast styling — Black pill bottom-center, auto-dismiss 2s. Matches the rest
   of the design (no fancy framework, just position-fixed). Tell me if you want
  it differently styled (e.g. matching the deep blue) or auto-dismiss timing
  changed.

       1  # Changelog

       3 +## Session 17.1 -- 2026-04-29 -- Hero density, layout balance, 
         +angular buttons, platform-aware share                          
       4 +- **Landing hero**: replaced the 6-mark tilted grid with a dens
         +e 12×3 grid of 36 generated samples at 100px each, gap-2 (8px),
         + no rotation. Wrapped in a full-width `overflow-hidden` contain
         +er with vertical padding (`py-8 md:py-12`); the hero now breaks
         + out of the page's `max-w-[700px]` constraint. Inner grid uses 
         +`w-max` so it sits at its natural ~1288px width and the edges g
         +et clipped on viewports narrower than that — the "infinite fiel
         +d" effect kicks in on most laptops and all mobile. Samples are 
         +generated by `buildSample(i)` using prime-modulo cycling on eac
         +h axis (medium / teachers / helpers / references / collaborator
         +s / AI fields) so adjacent cells rarely match.                 
       5 +- **Landing CTA**: reverted from `bg-[#3E51C0]` back to `bg-bla
         +ck`. Bumped to `h-12 px-6 text-lg` (48px tall, 24px horizontal 
         +padding, 18px text) with no border-radius — sharp corners to ma
         +tch the angular Tracemark language.                            
       6 +- **Landing data note**: removed the "How is your data used?" h
         +eading. The paragraph is now `text-base leading-relaxed` (16px,
         + default body color `#37352F`, not muted gray) with `mt-12` fro
         +m the CTA and `max-w-[600px]` centered. Reads as a continuation
         + of the page, not as fine print.                               
       7 +- **Result page two-column balance**: grid template changed fro
         +m `[minmax(0,440px)_1fr]` to `[6fr_4fr]` — left column is now ~
         +60% on desktop. Tracemark's `max-w-[540px]` lets it grow to fil
         +l the wider column. Column gap unchanged at 12 (48px).         
       8 +- **Result page Tracemark card**: the wrapping `ref` div now ca
         +rries `bg-[#F5F5F5] p-6 md:p-8` for a subtle gray "card" backdr
         +op. The bg is on the wrapper; the download function reads the i
         +nner SVG via `querySelector('svg')`, so the backdrop is display
         +-only and never captured in the PNG.                           
       9 +- **Result page caption**: new line below the Tracemark and but
         +tons — "This is your Tracemark. Each patch represents a differe
         +nt dimension of your creative process." (14px, `#666`, max-w-[4
         +40px] centered). On mobile it stacks between the buttons and th
         +e Grace section, matching the request to put it between Tracema
         +rk and Grace.                                                  
      10 +- **Result page spacing**: outer container `space-y-10` → `spac
         +e-y-16`; `main` padding `py-10 md:py-16` → `py-12 md:py-20`. Gr

⏺ Pushed as c2f9964.

  Summary

  1. Hero grid — Replaced the 6 tilted Tracemarks with a dense 12×3 grid of 36
  deterministically-generated samples at 100px each, gap-2 (8px), no rotation.
  Full-width overflow-hidden wrapper breaks out of max-w-[700px]; inner grid
  uses w-max so it sits at its natural ~1288px width and clips on viewports
  narrower than that. buildSample(i) uses prime-modulo cycling across each axis
  (medium, teachers, helpers, references, collaborators, AI fields) so adjacent
  cells rarely match.

  2. Result page two-column balance — Grid template [minmax(0,440px)_1fr] →
  [6fr_4fr] (~60/40 split). Left column gets the wider share; gap stays at 12
  (48px). Tracemark max-w-[540px] fills the wider column. New bg-[#F5F5F5] p-6 
  md:p-8 card behind the Tracemark (display-only — download captures only the
  inner SVG, never the card). New caption below buttons: "This is your 
  Tracemark. Each patch represents a different dimension of your creative 
  process." (14px #666, max-w-[440px] centered). On mobile the caption stacks
  between buttons and Grace.

  3. Buttons — angular and large — All three (CTA, Download, Share) are now h-12
   px-6 text-lg with no border-radius. Filled style is bg-black text-white.
  Outlined Share is border-[3px] border-black bg-transparent text-black. The
  toast pill also lost its rounded-full to match.

  4. Share button platform detection — useState initializer reads
  navigator.userAgent once at mount (the Suspense boundary above means this is
  client-only). Renders one of three inline SVGs: iOS = square + up arrow,
  Android = three connected dots, desktop = chain link. Label flips: Share on
  mobile, Copy link on desktop. The literal ↗ is gone.

  5. Result spacing — Outer container space-y-10 → space-y-16; main py-10 
  md:py-16 → py-12 md:py-20; Grace lines now leading-[1.8].

  6. Landing data note — Removed the "How is your data used?" heading. Paragraph
   is now text-base leading-relaxed (16px, default body color #37352F), mt-12
  from the CTA, max-w-[600px] centered. Reads as a continuation rather than fine
   print.

  7. CTA reverted to black — Per your instruction. The deep blue still appears
  on the Grace box's left accent and as a system color, just not on the buttons.

  Things to flag

  1. Hero edge-clipping behavior — The grid's natural width is 1288px (12×100 +
  11×8). Viewports < 1288px get visible cut-off; viewports ≥ 1288px (some larger
   desktops) will see the grid centered with whitespace on each side. If you
  want the cut-off effect on every screen including 1920+ desktops, bump the
  column count to 16 (1700px width) or scale up size. Current setting covers
  most laptops and all mobile.
  2. Hero on very narrow mobile — At 375px width with 1288px grid, ~228px of the
   grid is cut off on each side, leaving 4–5 columns visible. Looks dense and
  graphic but the marks become small relative to viewport. If too aggressive,
  swap size={100} to size={80} or reduce columns.
  3. buildSample(i) is deterministic — Same i always produces the same sample,
  so the grid is identical across SSR and client (no hydration mismatch) and
  stable across reloads. If you want randomness per visit, swap the modulos for
  a seeded random.
  4. Sticky left column on result — At md+, the Tracemark + buttons + caption
  stay pinned via md:sticky md:top-8 md:self-start while the grace scrolls. If a
   real submission's grace is short and fits within one viewport, sticky has no
  visible effect (nothing to scroll). Most graces are 5–9 lines + closing, so it
   kicks in.
  5. Share icon color — All three SVGs use currentColor, so they pick up the
  button's text-black. If you want a different icon color (e.g. blue inside the
  outlined button), it's a single class change on the button.
  6. Platform detection on cross-platform browsers — navigator.userAgent
  matching for iPhone|iPad|iPod and Android covers ~99% of mobile. iPad on
  iPadOS 13+ may report as Macintosh with touch — currently those land as
  desktop with Copy link. Tell me if you want a more aggressive mobile sniff.
  7. Toast styling — Lost rounded-full, now sharp-edged like everything else. If
   the angular pill feels weird as a toast, rounded-none removed easily.

  Summary

  0. Max-widths
  - Landing text content: 700px → 800px
  - Result two-column layout: 1000px → 1100px
  - Footer: 700px → 1100px (matches result)
  - Landing hero stays full-width
  - Mobile: full width with px-6 (unchanged)

  1. Hero grid — 8 cols × 2 rows = 16 marks at size={140}, gap-2. Natural width
  1176px (8×140 + 7×8). Overflow-hidden on the wrapper still clips edges on
  viewports under that width.

  2. Data transparency — Left-aligned now (mx-auto removed). Keeps mt-12,
  max-w-[600px], 16px default body color.

  3. Landing breathing room
  - Hero py-16 (64px above + below the grid)
  - Title mb-4 → subtitle
  - mt-10 → first body paragraph
  - Body paragraphs space-y-8
  - mt-12 → CTA
  - mt-12 → data note
  - Page bottom: pb-16 md:pb-20

  4. CTA full width — inline-flex h-12 w-full items-center justify-center gap-2 
  bg-black text-lg text-white, no border-radius, with the Lucide ArrowRight icon
   (size 20, strokeWidth 2.5) trailing the label.

  5. Grace styling
  - text-[13px] md:text-[15px], text-[#666], no italic
  - Grace box: border-l-2 border-black bg-[#F8F7F6]
  - Bold subjects: explicit <strong className="font-semibold text-[#37352F]"> so
   the inner text is semibold + darker than the surrounding muted body, no
  longer browser-default bold

  6. Buttons match Tracemark width — Wrapped in mx-auto mt-6 flex w-full 
  max-w-[540px] gap-2. Each button is flex-1, so they split the 540 width 50/50
  minus the 8px gap. Both h-12 text-lg, padding reduced from px-6 to px-4 (since
   flex-1 already provides width — px-6 would crowd the icon+label inside a
  flex-1 column).

  7. Result spacing
  - Title mb-8 md:mb-12
  - Tracemark card → buttons: mt-6
  - Buttons → caption: mt-4
  - Page padding: pt-12 md:pt-20 pb-20 (always 80px before footer)
  - Grace intro mb-6 before box
  - Grace lines space-y-4 md:space-y-5

  8. Caption text — Replaced with: "This is your Tracemark. Each patch maps a
  different part of how this piece was made: who taught you, what you soaked in,
   what tools you used, and who shaped it alongside you." Caption max-w bumped
  to 540px so it lines up under the Tracemark; centered.

  Build + lint clean.

  Things to flag

  1. Button content fit at narrow widths — At ~540px max-w split 50/50 with
  gap-2, each button has ~266px. "Download Tracemark" + 20px icon + 8px gap fits
   comfortably; "Copy link" / "Share" + icon fits trivially. On very narrow
  mobile (<540px viewport), the buttons share whatever's available. Reduced
  internal padding to px-4 to give the long label more room.
  2. Footer at 1100px on the landing page — Footer is in the layout so it
  inherits the same 1100px max-w on every page. On the landing page (text
  content at 800), the footer's centered text appears in a wider band than the
  body content above it. If that visual mismatch bothers you, we can use a
  per-page footer width or constrain footer to the smaller of the two; let me
  know.
  3. Bold subject color — text-[#37352F] is the default body color on most
  pages. Inside the grace box where surrounding text is #666, the subjects pop
  because they're darker AND semibold. If #37352F looks too close to the muted
  body in some lighting, switching to plain black text-black would make them
  more emphatic.
  4. Grace lines space-y-4 md:space-y-5 — That's 16/20px between lines on top of
   leading-[1.8] within each line. Spacious. If too airy, drop to space-y-3 
  md:space-y-4 (12/16px).
  5. Hero grid edge clipping — At 1176px natural width, viewports below ~1200px
  get visible cut-off. On 1440+ desktops, the grid centers with whitespace each
  side. The "sample field" effect will be most pronounced on laptop/mobile
  sizes.

⏺ Pushed as a98e277.

  Summary

  1. New MEDIUM_COLOR palette — Five shifts:
  - digital-2d: #F87014 → #3E51C0 (orange → deep blue)
  - sculpted: #CB7C2B → #E98FC6 (brown → pink)
  - printed: #E98FC6 → #7BD0FD (pink → light blue)
  - motion: #567550 → #8CBBA1 (dark → light green)
  - mixed-media: #8CBBA1 → #F87014 (light green → orange)
  - painted, 3d-digital, fiber, other unchanged

  2. Hero sample diversification — replaced the prime-modulo cycling with
  hand-tuned per-axis profiles:

  - Patch 1 (medium) — MEDIUMS[i % 9]. All 9 colors appear in the 16 samples
  (indices 0–8 cover every medium; 9–15 repeat).
  - Patch 3 (references) — REFERENCE_PROFILES is 16 distinct length-12 weight
  vectors. Each profile paints a different silhouette: artists-only, feeds-only,
   world-only, imagination-only, AI-only, uniform low, uniform full, alternating
   high/mid, scattered, etc.
  - Patch 6 (helpers) — HELPER_COUNTS = [0, 3, 1, 8, 5, 0, 11, 2, 4, 7, 0, 6, 1,
   9, 3, 0]. buildHelpers(i) picks count items from ALL_HELPERS at a
  prime-offset rotation. Some samples are entirely empty, some fill all 11
  cells.
  - Patch 7 (AI generator) — AI_USED_FLAGS alternates true/false in a
  non-uniform pattern. AI_KIND_SETS expanded from 4 to 8 entries with varied
  lengths (1–5 kinds), so the kinds-row density varies sample to sample.
  - Patch 8 (direction) — DIRECTIONS = [3, 8, 1, 6, 10, 4, 9, 2, 7, 5, 8, 1, 10,
   3, 6, 4]. All 1–10 values represented, with adjacent samples deliberately far
   apart (e.g. 3 → 8 → 1 → 6).
  - Patch 9 (collaborators) — COLLAB_COUNTS = [2, 0, 5, 1, 3, 7, 0, 4, 1, 2, 5, 
  3, 0, 4, 2, 6]. buildCollaborators(i) picks count from ALL_COLLABORATORS.
  Density ranges from 0 cells lit to all 7 lit.

  Build + lint clean.

  Things to flag

  1. Sample count vs profile count — REFERENCE_PROFILES and the *_COUNTS arrays
  each have exactly 16 entries, matching SAMPLES.length. Adjacent indices have
  deliberately different shapes, so no two neighboring marks should look the
  same in either the 4×3 mobile grid or the 8×2 desktop grid.
  2. Mobile shows 12 of the 16 — The mobile grid uses SAMPLES.slice(0, 12).
  Indices 0–11 cover the most varied profiles, so mobile gets a representative
  cross-section.
  3. Patch 7 row 1–4 density — When aiUsed=true, the kinds row varies from 1
  cell highlighted (just text-to-image) to 5 cells (the longest kind set).
  Combined with the alternating AI_USED_FLAGS pattern, every other sample either
   shows the full grid lit or pink-only.
  4. Patch 1 color map change — This affects every Tracemark on the site, not
  just the hero. If you want to revert any of the swaps (e.g. keep motion as the
   dark green it was), it's a one-line revert in the map.

  every pattern appears at least once across the 16 marks.

  - Wrapper changed from max-w-[65vh] to w-fit. The wrapper now shrinks to fit
  the Tracemark's actual rendered width, and the buttons row's w-full inside
  that wrapper inherits exactly the same span.

  3. Empty-Tracemark skeleton loading state
  - Removed the dashed-border placeholder div and the "Tracemark — loading…" /
  "awaiting submission" inline text.
  - The Tracemark always renders. Pre-load it gets data={} and shows the
  base-color skeleton (Patch 0 black, Patch 1 fallback #B5DD35 no pattern, Patch
   5 dark green, Patches 4/6/7/9 base colors, Patch 8 no bar). Once the
  submission resolves, it fills in.
  - Page-level "Loading your submission…" announcement above the two-column grid
   still handles the a11y signal.

  Things to flag

  1. Pattern asset count — verified public/patterns/ contains all 12
  pattern-*.svg files. The mapping is in place; if any individual SVG doesn't
  render correctly when the <image> loads, that's a pattern-asset issue not a
  code one.
  2. <image href="..."> is the modern SVG attribute (vs the deprecated
  xlink:href). Works in all current browsers and React 19's JSX. If you need to
  support very old Safari (<13), we'd need both attributes.
  3. w-fit browser support — width: fit-content is supported in all current
  browsers (Tailwind v4 generates it natively). On the rare browser without
  support, the wrapper would default to block-width and the buttons would still
  match — fine fallback.
  4. Skeleton visual — when data={}, the empty Tracemark looks visually
  distinctive enough to read as "this is your Tracemark, populating now." If
  you'd rather it look more obviously skeletal (e.g. faded), we can wrap in a
  div with opacity-60 while loading. Tell me if you want that.

  1. TRACEMARK SKELETON MODE (components/Tracemark.tsx)                         
                                                                                
     When data is empty (Object.keys(data).length === 0), render only           
     the stroke grid — no base color fills anywhere.                            
                                                                                
     Implementation pattern: wrap ALL fill-bearing content (every base          
     color rect, every selected-state rect, the Patch 1 pattern overlay,        
     the Patch 5 fill triangle, the Patch 8 direction bar, every                
     Patch 3 bar) in a single outer <g> with:                                   
                                                                                
       style={{ opacity: isSkeleton ? 0 : 1, transition: 'opacity 500ms         
  ease-out' }}                                                                  
                                                                                
     where const isSkeleton = !data || Object.keys(data).length === 0.          
                                                                                
     The stroke-only rects (patch boundaries, internal cell dividers)           
     render OUTSIDE that group so they're always visible. The Patch 5           
     diagonal line counts as a stroke and stays visible in skeleton mode.       
                                                                                
     Patch 0 (static black anchor) stays black in skeleton mode — render        
     it outside the opacity group too, so it identifies the mark as a           
     Tracemark even when empty.                                                 
                                                                                
     Net result: skeleton state shows the black anchor + the full grid          
     structure in black strokes on white. When data arrives, all the            
     fills fade in over 500ms.
