  Things to flag

  1. CSS transition on SVG <g> — style={{ opacity, transition }} on an SVG <g>
  is supported in all modern browsers. The transition triggers when React
  re-renders with a different opacity value, which happens when state.data
  populates and isSkeleton flips to false.
  2. Pre-cached graceState revisit — On a revisit where localStorage has a
  cached grace, the submission still has to fetch (it's not cached locally). The
   skeleton state will still appear briefly before the submission API responds.
  If you want to also cache the submission JSON in localStorage, that's a
  separate session.
  3. Patch 5 in skeleton — visible content is the patch border + the diagonal
  hypotenuse from (210,0) to (0,180). Reads as a triangle outline. When data
  arrives, the two polygons fade in behind the diagonal.
  4. Patch 1 in skeleton — empty (no medium fill, no seed pattern). Just the
  patch border. Once data arrives, both the medium-color rect AND the pattern
  overlay fade in together as part of the same opacity group.
  5. Skeleton on cells with structure — Patches 4, 6, 7, 9 in skeleton show the
  cell grid in black strokes only. Looks like an architectural drawing of the
  mark. Patches 3, 8 show their internal structure (5 sections / 6 columns) the
  same way. Visually distinct enough to read as a meaningful skeleton, not just
  "empty box."

⏺ Inspection findings

  I traced the overflow:

  1. SVG element (components/Tracemark.tsx): has width={size} and height={size}
  SVG attributes (default 540). The SVG's className is passed through from the
  caller — there's no baked-in max-w-full, so the SVG renders at its intrinsic
  540 unless the caller constrains it.
  2. Wrapper (app/result/page.tsx): <div className="w-fit">. w-fit sizes to
  content width with no max-w cap, so it grows to whatever the SVG renders at.
  3. Result page Tracemark className: "h-auto w-auto max-h-[65vh]". On a
  portrait phone (e.g. 375 × 800), 65vh = 520. The SVG height-caps at 520,
  aspect ratio carries width to 520, so the SVG ends up 520px wide on a 375px 
  viewport — exceeds the screen by ~145px.
  4. Page container (<main>): px-6 (24px each side). Doesn't help because the
  wrapper itself doesn't honor the parent's width.

  So the root cause is: w-auto SVG + w-fit wrapper + no max-w anywhere, with
  max-h-[65vh] driving the width via aspect ratio on portrait mobile.

  Fixes

  components/Tracemark.tsx — merge max-w-full h-auto into the SVG's default
  className so it always honors its parent's width:

  What was changed

  components/Tracemark.tsx — one line:
  - SVG className is now block h-auto max-w-full ${className ?? ''}. max-w-full
  ensures the SVG never exceeds its parent's width regardless of the caller.
  h-auto lets height auto-adjust via the viewBox aspect ratio.

  app/result/page.tsx — three lines:
  - Wrapper w-fit → w-full max-w-full md:w-fit. Mobile: fills the page column.
  Desktop: shrinks to fit content.
  - Tracemark className h-auto w-auto max-h-[65vh] → w-full md:w-auto 
  md:max-h-[65vh]. Mobile: w-full makes the SVG honor the wrapper's width with
  no height cap (height = width via aspect ratio). Desktop: w-auto returns to
  intrinsic-with-height-cap behavior.
  - Main padding px-6 → px-4 md:px-8. Tighter on mobile (more usable width);
  airier on desktop.

  Deviation from your literal spec

  You asked for width="100%" as an SVG attribute plus max-w-full h-auto in the
  className. I kept width={size} / height={size} attributes as-is and put the
  responsive behavior entirely in the className.

  Why: The landing hero renders 16 marks inside <div class="w-max grid 
  grid-cols-8"> and relies on each Tracemark having an intrinsic 140px width to
  drive grid cell sizing. With width="100%" and a w-max parent, the parent has
  no width to expand into → the SVG would collapse to a browser default
  (~300×150), and the hero would render at the wrong size.

  The CSS-only fix achieves the same goal (no overflow on mobile, scales down to
   viewport) without the hero collapse. If you'd prefer to follow the literal
  spec, I can refactor the hero to use grid-cols-[repeat(8,140px)] 
  grid-cols-[repeat(4,100px)] (explicit cell widths) so a width="100%" SVG works
   inside it. Tell me if you want that swap.

  ```ts                                                                         
     const rateLimits = new Map<string, number[]>();                            
     const WINDOW_MS = 60_000;                                                  
     const MAX_REQUESTS = 5;                                                    
                                                                                
     function getIP(req: Request): string {                                     
       const forwarded = req.headers.get('x-forwarded-for');                    
       if (forwarded) return forwarded.split(',')[0].trim();                    
       return req.headers.get('x-real-ip') ?? 'unknown';                        
     }                                                                          
                                                                                
     function checkRateLimit(ip: string): boolean {                             
       const now = Date.now();                                                  
       const timestamps = (rateLimits.get(ip) ?? []).filter(t => now - t <      
  WINDOW_MS);                                                                   
       if (timestamps.length >= MAX_REQUESTS) return false;                     
       timestamps.push(now);                                                    
       rateLimits.set(ip, timestamps);                                          
       return true;                                                             
     }
  ```                                                                           

⏺ Pushed as 92746ff.

  Summary

  1. Grace cache bust — localStorage key prefix grace-${sid} → grace-v2-${sid}
  in both read and write call sites. Existing pre-voice-rules graces are
  invalidated by key.

  2. Rate limit on /api/grace — Per-IP in-memory sliding window, 5 requests /
  60s. Returns 429 { error: 'Rate limited' } on overflow. Backstop trims the
  oldest half when the Map exceeds 1000 entries. IP from x-forwarded-for →
  x-real-ip → 'unknown'.

  3. Diagnostic log cleanup — Removed the [tally] sid=… mapped: console.log from
   app/api/tally-submission/route.ts. lib/tally.ts had no console.log statements
   — only console.warn for unmapped options/UUIDs/buckets, which I left in place
   per the strict instruction (and per instruction 4 explicitly preserving the
  unmapped-text warning).

  4. SEED_MAP "Other" + fallback — Added Other, Other..., Other…, and Other 
  (please specify) to SEED_TEXT_TO_SCHEMA so any Tally rendering matches. Plus
  defensive fallback in mapTallyToProvenance: non-empty unmapped seed text now
  falls back to 'other' (?? 'other') so the pattern overlay always picks a sane
  value. mapOne's console.warn still surfaces the unrecognized text.

  5. Result page layout — Replaced md:grid md:grid-cols-[6fr_4fr] md:gap-10 with
   flex flex-col md:flex-row md:gap-12. Left column md:flex-shrink-0 md:w-fit 
  md:sticky md:top-8 md:self-start. Right column md:flex-1 with grace content
  wrapped in mx-auto max-w-[600px] for a 600px reading-width cap that doesn't
  smear across wide viewports. Mobile keeps the existing stacked behavior.

  6. Changelog Session 19 entry added.

  Things to flag

  1. Rate limit memory — Map is module-scoped in a Next.js Function. Vercel's
  Fluid Compute reuses function instances across requests (so the Map persists
  for the warm container) but separate instances don't share state. With 5/60s
  per IP per instance, the effective limit can be a small multiple of that on
  busy traffic. For symposium prep this is fine; if you need strict cluster-wide
   limits, swap to Vercel KV or similar.
  2. Other (please specify) and ellipsis variants — I added all four common
  Tally renderings as map keys. The defensive fallback also catches anything we
  missed, mapping to 'other' and warning. So the seed-pattern overlay should
  never silently drop again.
  3. Sticky inside flex — md:sticky md:top-8 md:self-start on the left flex
  item. Sticky inside flex works as long as the cross-axis alignment isn't
  stretch (which would force the item to the parent's height). md:self-start
  overrides parent stretch, letting the section size to its content and stick
  within the viewport.
  4. max-w-[600px] on grace — On wide desktop viewports where the right flex
  column is e.g. ~600–900px wide, the grace caps at 600 and centers in the
  column. On narrower viewports (mobile), parent column is < 600 so the cap
  doesn't bind. Tell me if you'd rather it be wider (e.g. 700) or tighter
  (e.g. 540).
  5. localStorage cleanup — The old grace-${sid} keys still sit in users'
  browsers, taking up bytes until they get evicted by quota pressure. Not worth
  a cleanup pass — localStorage quota is typically 5–10 MB per origin and graces
   are tiny strings.

⏺ Pushed as 315ed0c.

  Summary

  Updated the <image> in Patch 1 with the oversize/offset attributes per spec:

  <image
    href={patternUrl}
    x={-2.11}
    y={-2.11}
    width={184.22}
    height={184.22}
    style={{ clipPath: 'inset(2.11px)' }}
  />

  The pattern asset's built-in border now overlays Patch 1's boundary stroke
  exactly — single visible border instead of duplicated nested ones.

  Note on clip-path

  You said "Patch 1 already has clip-path constraining content to its bounds."
  That isn't actually present in the current code — Patch 1 is a <g> with a fill
   rect and the image, no clipping. Without clipping, the oversized image would
  leak ~2.11px into Patch 0 (left) and Patch 3 (right).

  I added style={{ clipPath: 'inset(2.11px)' }} directly on the <image> element
  to satisfy the visual goal you described. CSS inset(2.11px) is
  element-relative: with the image bounding box at (-2.11, -2.11)–(182.11,
  182.11), inset 2.11 from each side leaves visible area (0, 0)–(180, 180),
  which is exactly Patch 1's bounds.

  Used CSS clip-path rather than <clipPath> element ID-references because the
  hero renders 16 Tracemark SVGs on a single page, and shared SVG IDs across
  them would compound — element-relative CSS sidesteps that.

  Build + lint clean.

⏺ Pushed as 4c7d022.

  Summary

  1. Site header
  - New components/SiteHeader.tsx — <header className="pt-6 pl-6 md:pt-8 
  md:pl-8"> containing a <Link href="/"> with the wordmark Creative Trace,
  text-base text-[#37352F] no-underline hover:underline. Inter is inherited from
   the body.
  - Imported into app/result/page.tsx. Rendered as the first element of
  ResultPage's return, outside the <Suspense> boundary so it's always visible
  (no client hooks). Sits above <main> for clean semantics.
  - Landing page (/) intentionally unchanged — the wordmark already exists as
  the hero title there.

  2. Mobile hero bleed symmetry
  - Replaced the two mx-auto w-max grids with a single flex justify-center
  wrapper containing both breakpoint grids.
  - Why it was bleeding right-only: mx-auto on a w-max element bigger than its
  parent computes both auto margins as 0, leaving the element flush-left and
  overflowing right. flex justify-center instead centers the overflowing child
  by negative-positioning, so equal amounts bleed off each side.
  - overflow-hidden on the outer band still clips the bleed.

  Note on width: 100vw

  Your spec said the hero container should be 100vw "to escape any parent
  max-width constraint." I kept it at w-full (its current behavior — full width
  of the unconstrained parent <main>) for two reasons:

  1. No max-w to escape: <main> has no max-w-* class, and the inner content's
  max-w lives on a sibling div, not on main. The hero is already
  full-viewport-width via w-full.
  2. w-screen risks horizontal scrollbar: 100vw includes the scrollbar gutter;
  the body's content area excludes it. On platforms with classic scrollbars,
  w-screen makes the hero ~17px wider than the body, causing a horizontal
  scrollbar. The overflow-hidden on the hero clips its own children but doesn't
  suppress this body-level overflow. The standard fix (overflow-x: hidden on
  body) would break the result page's position: sticky Tracemark column, since
  sticky requires a scrolling ancestor with non-hidden overflow.

  If <main> ever gains a max-w constraint, the literal full-bleed pattern is
  className="ml-[calc((100%-100vw)/2)] w-screen overflow-hidden". Easy retrofit.

  Build + lint clean.

  1. CREATE app/result/opengraph-image.tsx                                      
     Use Next.js 16's opengraph-image convention. The file exports a            
     default async function that returns ImageResponse from next/og.            
                                                                                
     Dimensions: 1200×630 (standard OG, also covers Twitter cards).             
     Runtime: 'edge' for fast generation.                                       
     Content type: image/png (default for ImageResponse).                       
                                                                                
     The function signature:                                                    
                                                                                
  ```ts                                                                         
     import { ImageResponse } from 'next/og';                                   
                                                                                
     export const runtime = 'edge';                                             
     export const alt = 'Your Creative Trace Tracemark';                        
     export const size = { width: 1200, height: 630 };                          
     export const contentType = 'image/png';                                    
                                                                                
     export default async function Image({                                      
       searchParams                                                             
     }: {                                                                       
       searchParams: { sid?: string }                                           
     }) {                                                                       
       // ...                                                                   
     }                                                                          
  ```                                                                           
                                                                                
     Logic:                                                                     
     - Read sid from searchParams. If missing, render a generic OG              
       showing a sample Tracemark with the wordmark.                            
     - If present, fetch the submission via the existing tally flow.            
       Since edge runtime can call fetch directly, hit                          
       `${process.env.VERCEL_URL ??                                             
  'http://localhost:3000'}/api/tally-submission?sid=${sid}`                     
       internally. Handle fetch failure by falling back to the generic OG.      
     - Render the Tracemark as inline SVG inside a JSX layout. The              
       ImageResponse renderer supports a subset of CSS via Satori. It           
       handles inline SVG, flexbox, basic positioning. It does NOT              
       support external image refs (the pattern <image href> tags),             
       so Patch 1's pattern overlay needs special handling — see below.         
                                                                                
  2. PATTERN HANDLING IN OG                                                     
     The Tracemark component uses <image href="/patterns/pattern-X.svg">        
     for Patch 1's seed pattern. Satori does not load external SVG refs.        
                                                                                
     Two options, pick the simpler one:                                         
     a) For the OG only, omit the pattern overlay. Patch 1 renders as           
        solid color. Acceptable visual sacrifice for the link preview.          
     b) Inline the pattern SVG content. At edge runtime, fetch the              
        pattern file as text, parse out the inner content, inline it            
        into the JSX. More work, more accurate.                                 
                                                                                
     Go with (a) for the first pass. Simpler, faster, ships tonight.            
     The mark still reads as distinctive in a 1200×630 preview because          
     the other 8 patches carry most of the visual identity.                     
                                                                                
     Add a TODO comment noting the pattern omission for phase 2.

⏺ Pushed as d481fc8.

  Summary

  1. app/result/opengraph-image.tsx (new) — Next.js 16 file-convention OG
  renderer:
  - Edge runtime, 1200×630 PNG
  - Reads sid from searchParams; fetches /api/tally-submission?sid=... via
  https://${process.env.VERCEL_URL} (or localhost:3000 in dev) and renders the
  actual Tracemark
  - Falls back to a hardcoded SAMPLE_DATA when no sid or the fetch fails —
  preview still looks like a Creative Trace mark
  - Inline TracemarkSVG duplicates the patch geometry/colors/JSX from
  components/Tracemark.tsx (Satori works best with self-contained markup; no
  React state/transitions to share)
  - Layout: white 1200×630, two-column flex. Left = Tracemark in 630×630 with
  45px padding; right = wordmark (48px, weight 700, #37352F) + tagline (24px,
  #666) at top, piece description for: <desc> (18px italic, #999) at
  bottom-right when present

  2. Patch 1 pattern omitted in OG (TODO phase 2) — Satori doesn't load external
   <image href> refs. Patch 1 in OG is a solid medium color. Other 8 patches
  carry the visual identity. Marked TODO near the file header for the
  inline-pattern follow-up.

  3. Result page refactored client → server for generateMetadata to coexist:
  - app/result/result-content.tsx (new, 'use client') — all the previous
  fetch/grace/download/share logic
  - app/result/page.tsx (server) — exports generateMetadata (title, description,
   openGraph.images, twitter.card: summary_large_image) plus the default
  ResultPage which renders <SiteHeader /> + <Suspense> around <ResultContent />
  - metadataBase resolves to https://${VERCEL_URL} on Vercel,
  http://localhost:3000 in dev — kills the build warning and gives social
  crawlers absolute URLs

  4. New route: /result/opengraph-image registered as a dynamic edge function in
   the build output.

  Build + lint clean.

  Things to flag

  1. Pattern overlay omitted in OG — Phase-2 path is to fetch each pattern SVG
  file as text at edge runtime, parse out the inner content, inline as JSX
  children. Roughly 50 LOC and a Map<SeedType, string> of cached SVG strings.
  Backlog candidate after symposium.
  2. Custom-domain OG URL — metadataBase uses VERCEL_URL (the *.vercel.app
  deployment URL) rather than creativetrace.art. Crawlers will see og:image URLs
   pointing to *.vercel.app even when the page itself was loaded from
  creativetrace.art. Both serve the same image, but the URL mismatch is slightly
   inconsistent. To force creativetrace.art, hardcode it in the prod branch
  (process.env.VERCEL_ENV === 'production' ? 'https://creativetrace.art' : ...).
   Easy follow-up if needed.
  3. Edge-runtime fetch latency — the OG renderer makes a fetch to
  /api/tally-submission inside the edge function. That's two hops per OG
  generation: crawler → edge OG handler → edge tally-submission handler → Tally
  API. Most crawlers timeout at 5–10s; should comfortably fit. If Tally is slow
  we'd see fallbacks to SAMPLE_DATA.
  4. No font loading — system font fallback. Wordmark + tagline use whatever
  Satori chooses (typically Helvetica-equivalent). If the typography mismatch
  with the live site bothers you, we'd add fonts: [{ name: 'Inter', data: ..., 
  weight: 400 }] to the ImageResponse opts and fetch the Inter binary. Adds
  ~100KB to the edge function cold start.
  5. Caching — social crawlers (Facebook/Twitter especially) cache OG images
  aggressively. After a deploy, force-refresh via
  https://www.opengraph.xyz/url/... or Twitter card validator. iMessage caches
  per-thread; test in a fresh thread.
  6. Build output shows ƒ /result/opengraph-image — the route is registered.
  Hitting https://creativetrace.art/result/opengraph-image?sid=X54LzlP directly
  returns the PNG, useful for debugging.

  2. BACKLOG: DARK MODE                                                         
     Add a new section in docs/backlog.md under visual polish or design         
     (whichever section exists; create a "Design system" section if             
     neither does):                                                             
                                                                                
     ### Dark mode support                                                      
                                                                                
     Adding dark mode is not a CSS variable swap for this project. The          
     Tracemark palette is calibrated against a white background. Light          
     fills (fiber #E6D4DA, blush, sky blue) carry visual weight on white        
     that disappears or reads muddy on dark. Pattern SVGs use black             
     strokes that vanish on dark unless inverted, and CSS filter inversion      
     introduces anti-alias artifacts. The Grace box's #F8F7F6 background        
     is calibrated to be subtle on white and would be glaring on dark.          
                                                                                
     Real implementation requires:                                              
     - Contrast-test every patch color and decide which fills need              
       dark-mode equivalents                                                    
     - Decide whether the Tracemark itself inverts or stays constant            
       (recommend constant — the mark should feel like a logo, not a            
       theme element)                                                           
     - Redesign the Grace box for dark surfaces                                 
     - Decide whether the Tracemark sits on a light card-within-dark-page       
       or directly on dark background                                           
     - Pattern SVG handling: either generate a parallel set with white          
       strokes, or accept the CSS filter quality cost                           
                                                                                
     Estimated as a multi-session design + implementation pass, not a           
     single prompt. Defer until project gets traction beyond symposium.         
                                                                                
  Do NOT touch lib/schema.ts, lib/tally.ts, components/Tracemark.tsx,           
  or any /api routes.
